name: Faster inbox triage in the panel

pr.title: Collapse the inbox's questions or notices from the header's counts
pr.head: 58ed764fd7d562ea3616bedc1feb4858a5c4863c

summary: Projector's panel sits above Claude Code's prompt. It lists your pull requests, then your inbox: questions an agent asked you and notices it told you, newest first. Its first line, the header, counts the open pull requests, questions, and notices.

When several sessions post at once, a burst of notices can push the questions, the items waiting on your answer, out of view. This change makes each item count in the header a button. Pressing 1 notice hides every notice and puts one line, - 1 notice, at the top of the list in the notice color. Pressing that line, or the count again, brings the notices back. Questions and notices collapse separately.

The collapsed kinds live in session state, so a new notice that arrives while notices are collapsed stays hidden and only raises the count. A kind with nothing open has no count in the header, so there would be nothing to press to expand it; while that holds, its muted items show.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Kind: an inbox item is a question or a notice.
  • Open: an item that is not answered and not snoozed. Only open items are counted.
  • Muted: a resolved or snoozed item, drawn in subtle gray.
  • Drawer: the detail view an item opens into, which takes the whole panel.

groups.title: Collapsing a kind in the panel
groups.kicker: The header's counts become buttons, and a collapsed kind becomes one line
intro: The panel's render handler in hooks/register.tsx draws the header and the list on every redraw. It now reads a new session atom, panelCollapsed, which holds the kinds you collapsed, and declares its type in hooks/types.d.ts.

isCollapsed(kind) is true only while the kind is in that list and the header has a count for it. That second condition is what lets the muted items show when a kind has nothing open: with no count, nothing on screen could expand the kind. fold(kind) toggles the kind in the atom, the action both the count and the expand line run.

The header was one Text. When it counts items it is now a row: a Text holding the name, the padding, and the pull request count, then each item count as a plain Button, then the age. The pieces add up to the same string as before, so the header still ends at the panel's edge.

files.note: Adds the collapse state, the header row of count buttons, and the expand lines at the top of the item list.

checks.text: isCollapsed also requires a count for the kind, so a kind with nothing open shows its muted items instead of an expand line nobody could reach from the header.

The header row's pieces add up to the old status string: the edited test asks through the tool, and the panel lists the question below the pull requests asserts the header still matches its text and ends at the panel's edge, and claude plugin test . passes.
The header's count buttons come before the pull request lines, so they are the first things the keyboard focus ring can reach. The review asks whether that order is intended.

files.note: Declares the panelCollapsed session state as a list of item kinds.

checks.text: hooks/typecheck.sh passes, and fails at the collapsed atom when this line is removed, so the declaration is what types it.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: One new test for collapsing, and the header read through a helper
intro: Because the header is now a row of pieces whenever it counts items, the existing tests can no longer find it as a single Text. A new helper, headerOf, reads the text of the element keyed header, and every header assertion uses it.

The new test walks the whole feature: collapse notices, collapse questions apart from them, expand from the line and from the count, dismiss the last notice so its kind shows again, then post a new notice and see it collapse.

files.note: Adds headerOf and the collapse test, and moves the header assertions onto the helper.
